newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer to cut more jobs in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Bayer to cut more jobs in Germany.

text.p: Chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG confirmed on Saturday that it wanted to cut its annual personnel costs by over a billion marks by 2000 by axeing 1,000 jobs a year at its five German plants.
A company spokesman said, however, that there would be no forced layoffs as part of the jobs reduction scheme.

The package of measures, presented by personnel director Hans-Juergen Mohr to a closed staff meeting last week, should save 300 million marks ($177.1 million) each year through job cuts and voluntary reduction of bonuses.
According to the plans, Bayer will guarantee to maintain its training programme and confirm its research and investment budgets for operations in Germany.
Bayer posted record profits of 2.7 billion marks last year but is seeking to cut costs at home and diversify abroad to remain globally competitive. ($ = 1.693 German Marks)
